e.title: PROOF 协议：「我们不判断什么是真的」——把主张、证据、签名与状态分层，且签名只证明密钥控制而不证明主张为真
e.title_en: The PROOF protocol: "we do not decide what is true" — layering claims, evidence, signatures and status, where a signature proves key control rather than the truth of the claim
e.title_hk: PROOF 協議：「我們不判斷什麼是真的」——把主張、證據、簽名與狀態分層，且簽名只證明密鑰控制而不證明主張為真
e.summary: 一个用于机器可读主张、证据、证明、时间上下文与验证生命周期的开放协议：一条记录把主张（主语＋谓词＋宾语）、证据、Ed25519 证明签名与状态打包在一起，并由「不变内容」的 SHA-256 决定其身份，因此改状态不会改身份；它开篇即声明自己不判断什么为真，并提供一整节「PROOF 不主张什么」，其中明确签名证明的是密钥控制与数据完整性而非主张为真
e.summary_hk: 一個用於機器可讀主張、證據、證明、時間上下文與驗證生命週期的開放協議：一條記錄把主張（主語＋謂詞＋賓語）、證據、Ed25519 證明簽名與狀態打包在一起，並由「不變內容」的 SHA-256 決定其身份，因此改狀態不會改身份；它開篇即聲明自己不判斷什麼為真，並提供一整節「PROOF 不主張什麼」，其中明確簽名證明的是密鑰控制與資料完整性而非主張為真
e.summary_en: An open protocol for machine-readable claims, evidence, attestations, temporal context and verification lifecycle: a record packages a claim (subject, predicate, object) with its evidence, an Ed25519 attestation signature and a status, and its identity is the SHA-256 of the immutable content alone so that changing status does not change identity; it states at the outset that it does not decide what is true, and carries a whole section on what PROOF does not claim, including that a signature proves key control and data integrity rather than the truth of the claim
e.body:
**PROOF** 是一个**用于机器可读主张、证据、证明与验证生命周期的开放协议**（仓库 `bhayrv/proof`），**实测 Apache-2.0 许可（`LICENSE` 于 main 分支实测 200）、★2、主语言 Python、仓库体量 651 KB、创建与最后推送均为 2026-09-09**（**许可、★数与语言等元数据经 GitHub 搜索 API 实测；`LICENSE` 经 raw 探测实测 200；均在解冻窗口内**）；**README 实测 8,060 字节**。**⚠️ 本条目需在开头写清一处范围问题**：**此处的「claims」指**机器可读的主张／断言**，**而非保险理赔**；**该协议**并非保险专用**，**其与保险行业的关系属**推断**（**证据随主张同行、AI 输出可被第三方独立核验**）**——**本词条不主张其与保险存在任何直接渊源**（**详见下方标注 ①**）。本条目属于本轮主题**「分开『我看到了什么』与『我因此断定什么』」**中的**第三种，也是唯一把这条界线**写成了协议本身的第一原则**的一种**。

可核实信息（**均 README 逐字实测**）：**标题逐字为「PROOF Protocol」**，**全称逐字为「**Protocol for Readable Object Origin and Facts**」**，**定位逐字为**：**「An open protocol for machine-readable claims, evidence, attestations, temporal context, and verification lifecycle.」**。⭐⭐⭐ **其开篇第二句逐字，是本条目最重要的一句**：**「**PROOF does not decide what is true.** It provides a portable structure that allows **independent systems to evaluate claims and their supporting evidence**.」**——**即「**PROOF 不判断什么为真**。它提供一种可移植的结构，让**彼此独立的系统去评估主张及其支撑证据**」**；**其更简短的一句口号逐字为**：**「> **Evidence should travel with information.**」**。**其状态逐字为**：**「**PROOF 0.2 — Development**」**，**并逐字声明**：**「This is an **experimental protocol and reference implementation**. It is **not yet a finalized interoperability standard**. Breaking changes may occur between development versions.」**。

对 RIAA：**① ⭐⭐⭐ **「PROOF does not decide what is true」是本条目最重要的一句，也是本轮主题的**最强形式****——**其余三条把界线划在**系统内部**（机器学习只负责感知、大模型只负责写文案、规则引擎负责判定）；**而本条把界线划在了**协议层**：**协议**只负责搬运与保真**，**判断留给**独立的、可能彼此不一致的消费者****。⭐⭐ **对做 AI 治理或理赔系统的学生，这是一种**把「工具」与「裁判」分开**的设计姿态**——**它使同一批记录可以被不同机构按各自政策评估，而不必信任同一个中枢**（**⚠️ 本词条**不主张**该姿态在实务中一定可行**——**本次未读其规范正文**）。**② ⭐⭐⭐ **「What PROOF Does NOT Claim」一整节逐字实测，是本会话见到**对新技术的自我限定写得最完整**的一份**——**四条逐字为**：**「PROOF does not determine universal or factual truth.」**；**「**A cryptographic signature proves key control and data integrity — not that the claim is true.**」**；**「PROOF does not require blockchain, tokens, or centralized services.」**；**「PROOF is an open infrastructure protocol, not an application.」**⭐⭐⭐ **第二条尤其值得单独记住**：**「密码学签名证明的是**密钥控制与数据完整性**，**而不是主张为真**」**——**在一个极易把「已签名」误读为「已证实」的语境里，这是一句必要的澄清**（**可与第 330 轮 [[claim-to-confidence]] 的「负向测试（agent identity denied）」、第 331 轮 [[aida-tix-anomaly-detection]] 的「一致性而非准确率」并读**——**三者都在切断一种**看起来像证明的东西**与**真正想要的结论**之间的联系****）。**③ ⭐⭐⭐ **「VERIFIED 表示『被某一指定的验证政策接受』，而不是普遍真理」是本条目在语义设计上最精确的一处**——**其状态生命周期逐字为**：**`UNKNOWN → OBSERVED → CORROBORATED → VERIFIED`**，**另有三个分支**：**`→ CONTESTED`、`→ RETRACTED`、`→ SUPERSEDED`**；**并逐字注明**：**「`VERIFIED` means "accepted by a specified verification policy" — not universal truth.」**；**另有一句逐字**：**「**Verification distinguishes cryptographic validity from factual truth.**」**⭐⭐ **对做核保或合规的同学，「谁的政策、什么时候的政策」决定了「已验证」是什么意思**——**这一点在保险的场景判定（如是否构成全损、是否属于承保事故）中同样成立**（**⚠️ 本词条**不主张**该状态机适用于任何保险流程**）。**④ ⭐⭐⭐ **「身份只由不变内容决定，改状态不改身份」是本条目在数据建模上最值得记的一点**——**逐字为**：**「The PROOF identity is a SHA-256 hash of the canonical representation of the **immutable content** only: Protocol version (`"proof": "0.2"`), Claim (subject, predicate, object), Evidence records. **Mutable fields (status, observed_at, attestations) are excluded. Changing status does not change identity.**」**⭐⭐⭐ **对做审计或版本化的学生，这是一条**清晰的不变量**：**「这条主张是什么」与「它现在被如何对待」是两件事**，**后者可反复更改而前者不变**（**可与第 331 轮 [[paco-uw]] 的「历史表永不复写」并读——**两者都靠**把可变与不可变分开**来支撑可审计性**；**⚠️ 本词条**不主张**该设计在所有场景都适用**——**例如证据被追加时身份会变，**本次未核实其版本迁移做法**）。**⑤ ⭐⭐⭐ **「互相矛盾的主张可以并存」被写进了关系类型**——**其图关系逐字为**：**`supports` / `corroborates`（正向证据连接）**；**「`contradicts` — **conflicting claims (both can coexist)**」**；**`supersedes`（更新版本）**；**`derived_from`（来源链）****；**另有一句逐字**：**「A PROOF record packages the claim with its supporting evidence, cryptographic signatures from those who attest to it, and a traceable lifecycle. It represents exactly what was claimed, what evidence was associated with it, who attested to the **exact immutable payload**, and **what supports or contradicts it**.」**⭐⭐⭐ **「互相矛盾的主张可以并存」与第 331 轮 [[paco-uw]] 的「两种求值策略的结果即使互相矛盾也都留着」是同一种态度**——**即**不把矛盾消解掉，而是把它记录下来****（**⚠️ 本词条**不主张**该设计能解决证据冲突**——**它只是**不让冲突消失****）。**⑥ ⭐⭐⭐ **`demo_ai_agent_pipeline.py` 这一示例是本条目与**AI 治理**最直接相关的一处**——**逐字为**：**「`demo_ai_agent_pipeline.py` — Simulates an AI extraction workflow: mock extraction → evidence association → review → attestation → deterministic verification, **allowing downstream systems to verify the claimed provenance and attestation integrity without trusting the AI model itself**.」**⭐⭐⭐ **「无需信任 AI 模型本身，下游系统即可核验其所声称的来源与证明完整性」**——**这与本站连续多轮的主题高度同源**（**第 329 轮 [[reinsurance-treaty-agent]] 的逐字段 grounding 回查、第 330 轮 [[claim-to-confidence]] 的独立 oracle 与只增不改审计日志、第 331 轮 [[aida-tix-anomaly-detection]] 的「基准被刻意排除在特征矩阵外」**）；**本条提供的是**标准化的形式**（**⚠️ 本词条**不主张**该示例已实现或可运行**——**本次未运行**）。**⑦ ⭐⭐ **其余三个示例逐字实测且都与「主张会随时间变化」有关**：**`demo_financial_intelligence.py`**（**一条盈利主张、多条证据、一份证明、以及**后来一条相矛盾的主张**及其 `contradicts` 关系**）**；**`demo_temporal_supersession.py`**（**一条收购主张被修订及 `supersedes` 关系**，**并逐字说明「how a machine can trace claim history and **apply an explicit consumer policy to identify the currently preferred claim**」**）；**`visualizer/index.html`**（**无依赖的 HTML／JS 图可视化**）**；**`cli_end_to_end.ps1`**（**完整 CLI 生命周期的 PowerShell 脚本**）。**⑧ ⭐⭐ **安全模型一节逐字，且含三条与「别把签名当真相」互补的限定**：**「Signatures prove key control and data integrity, not factual truth.」**；**「**Private keys are never persisted by the library.**」**；**「**Timestamps are self-reported metadata, not cryptographically bound.**」**；**「The protocol is experimental.」**⭐⭐ **第三条值得单独记**：**时间戳是**自报元数据、并非密码学绑定****——**即「某人在某时说」这件事本身并不被密码学保证**（**对做审计追踪的同学，这是一个容易被忽略的薄弱环节**）。**⑨ ⭐⭐ **互操作性一节逐字列出了六个真实标准，是本条目在标准生态上最可核实的一处**：**`docs/interoperability.md` 逐字为「How PROOF maps to **W3C PROV, C2PA, Verifiable Credentials, Sigstore, in-toto, and Schema.org**」**；**另有 `docs/architecture.md`（**含不变身份模型与规范化策略**）与 **`spec/PROOF.md`（**规范正文**）**⭐⭐ **这些是**可被独立查证**的既有标准名**（**⚠️ 本词条**不主张**其映射准确或完整**——**本次未读该文档**）。**⑩ ⭐ **CLI 与 Python API 逐字实测且都强调**严格的管道兼容性****：**CLI 含 `proof create`（`--subject`／`--predicate`／`--object`／`--evidence-type`／`--evidence-source`）、`proof inspect`、`proof identity`、`proof keygen`、`proof sign --private-key`、`proof verify`**，**并逐字说明「All commands support **JSON input/output for strict pipeline compatibility**.」**；**Python API 含 `Claim`、`Evidence`、`Proof`、`proof_id`、`create_attestation`、`verify_attestation`、`verify_proof`、`Attestation` 与 `result.to_dict()`**；**要求 Python 3.11+**。**⑪ ⭐ **版本参与身份计算这一细节逐字**：**「The version participates in identity computation — **the same claim under different versions has different identities**.」**——**⚠️ 对一个自述**仍会破坏性变更**的实验性协议而言，这意味着**跨版本的身份不稳定****（**本词条**不主张**其适合作为长期归档标识**）。**⑫ ⭐ 可与本站溯源、审计与 AI 治理条目并读**：[[claim-to-confidence]]、[[insurance-governance]]、[[reproducible-actuarial-work]]、[[verified-reserving]]、[[rag-assurance]]、[[powmcp-skills]]、[[underwriting-decision-safety]]、[[brel-xbrl]]、[[risk-data-library-standard]]。

⚠️ **如实标注**：**① ⚠️ **范围必须写清**：**该仓库是一个**通用**的机器可读主张与证据溯源协议**，**不是保险工具**，**README 全文**未提及保险**；**其在此处的相关性由**本词条推断**——**即「证据随主张同行」与「下游可不信任 AI 模型而核验来源」这两点对理赔证据链与 AI 输出审计具有一般意义**；**本词条明确标注该相关性为推断，不主张其与保险行业存在任何直接渊源、适配或已被采用**；**②** 本次核实的是**仓库元数据（部分经 GitHub 搜索 API）、README（8,060 字节）全文的定义段、状态声明、问题陈述、核心数据模型、四条「不主张」、状态生命周期、身份计算、图关系、Quickstart、Python API、示例清单、开发与安全模型、版本化、架构／互操作性／规范指引与许可**，**并以 raw 探测确认 `LICENSE` 存在（HTTP 200）**，⭐⭐ **但**未克隆、未安装、未运行其 CLI 或 Python API、未运行 `pytest`、未读 `spec/PROOF.md` 与 `docs/` 下任何文档、未运行任何示例、未打开其可视化器、未读 `SECURITY.md` 与任何源码****，因此**不能转述其规范化策略、签名与验证的实现细节、图关系的数据结构或其任何输出**；**② ⭐⭐⭐ **未核实**「PROOF does not decide what is true」这一自我定位在实现中是否成立**——**例如其 `verify_proof` 是否确实只做密码学与政策判定而不引入任何语义判断**；**本次未读源码**；**这是本条目最需要后续核实的一处**；**③ ⭐⭐⭐ **未核实**其身份不变量「改状态不改身份」在实现中是否成立**，**亦未核实**「版本参与身份计算」与「证据被追加后身份如何变化」的实际行为**；**④ ⭐⭐ **未核实**其与 W3C PROV、C2PA、Verifiable Credentials、Sigstore、in-toto 与 Schema.org 的映射是否准确或完整**（**本次未读 `docs/interoperability.md`**）；**⑤ ⭐⭐ **未核实**其 Ed25519 签名、密钥管理与时间戳处理的实现是否安全**——**⚠️ 其自述**私钥从不持久化**、**时间戳为自报且非密码学绑定**；**本词条**不主张**其可抵御任何特定威胁**（**本次未做任何安全评估**）；**⑥ ⭐⭐ **未核实**其四个示例（尤其 `demo_ai_agent_pipeline.py`）是否可运行或确如描述**；**⑦ ⭐ ⚠️ **该协议自述为**「PROOF 0.2 — Development」且**「not yet a finalized interoperability standard」**、**「Breaking changes may occur」**、**「The protocol is experimental」****——**本词条据此**不主张**其适合作为任何生产系统、长期归档或合规存档的基础**；**⑧ ⭐ ⚠️ **未核实**其 Apache-2.0 许可下的专利授权条款与贡献者政策**（**本次未读 `LICENSE` 正文与 `CONTRIBUTING` 类文件**）；**⑨ ⭐ ★2、fork 数本次未核实**（**核心 API 于本轮触及速率上限，该字段以搜索 API 结果为准**）；**关注度极低**，**不主张其成熟度、安全性或已被采用**；**⑩ ⭐ **无 topics 信息本次未获取**（**搜索 API 未返回 `topics` 字段**）——**本词条不主张其 topics 为何**；**⑪ 是否有中文材料本次未核实**（**README 实测为英文**）。**核实说明**：`bhayrv/proof` 的许可、★数与语言等元数据经 GitHub **搜索** API 于 2026-09-11 实测取得（**核心 API 于本轮触及速率上限，故未逐一读取 repo 端点**）；README 8,060 字节经 `raw.githubusercontent.com` 实测逐字核对；`LICENSE` 经 raw 探测确认存在（HTTP 200）；**未克隆、未安装、未运行、未读规范与源码**。
e.body_hk:
**PROOF** 是一個**用於機器可讀主張、證據、證明與驗證生命週期的開放協議**（倉庫 `bhayrv/proof`），**實測 Apache-2.0 許可（`LICENSE` 於 main 分支實測 200）、★2、主語言 Python、體量 651 KB、創建與最後推送均為 2026-09-09**（**許可、★數與語言等元數據經 GitHub 搜索 API 實測；均在解凍窗口內**）；**README 實測 8,060 位元組**。**⚠️ 本條目需在開頭寫清一處範圍問題**：**此處的「claims」指**機器可讀的主張／斷言**，**而非保險理賠**；**該協議**並非保險專用**，**其與保險行業的關係屬**推斷****——**不主張其與保險存在任何直接淵源**。本條目屬本輪主題**「分開『我看到了什麼』與『我因此斷定什麼』」**中的**第三種，也是唯一把這條界線**寫成了協議本身的第一原則**的一種**。

可核實資訊（**均 README 逐字實測**）：**標題逐字「PROOF Protocol」**，**全稱逐字「**Protocol for Readable Object Origin and Facts**」**，**定位逐字**：**「An open protocol for machine-readable claims, evidence, attestations, temporal context, and verification lifecycle.」**。⭐⭐⭐ **開篇第二句逐字，是本條目最重要的一句**：**「**PROOF does not decide what is true.** It provides a portable structure that allows **independent systems to evaluate claims and their supporting evidence**.」**；**其口號逐字**：**「> **Evidence should travel with information.**」**。**狀態逐字**：**「**PROOF 0.2 — Development**」**，**並逐字聲明**「This is an **experimental protocol and reference implementation**. It is **not yet a finalized interoperability standard**. Breaking changes may occur between development versions.」**。

對 RIAA：**① ⭐⭐⭐ **「PROOF does not decide what is true」是本輪主題的**最強形式****——**其餘三條把界線劃在**系統內部**（機器學習只管感知、大模型只管寫文案、規則引擎負責判定）；**而本條把界線劃在了**協議層**：**協議**只負責搬運與保真**，**判斷留給**獨立的、可能彼此不一致的消費者****（**⚠️ 不主張**該姿態在實務中一定可行**）。**② ⭐⭐⭐ **「What PROOF Does NOT Claim」一整節逐字，是本會話見到**對新技術的自我限定寫得最完整**的一份**——**四條逐字**：「PROOF does not determine universal or factual truth.」；**「**A cryptographic signature proves key control and data integrity — not that the claim is true.**」**；「PROOF does not require blockchain, tokens, or centralized services.」；「PROOF is an open infrastructure protocol, not an application.」**⭐⭐⭐ **第二條尤其值得單獨記住**：**「密碼學簽名證明的是**密鑰控制與資料完整性**，而不是主張為真」**——**在一個極易把「已簽名」誤讀為「已證實」的語境裡，這是必要的澄清**（可與第 330 輪 [[claim-to-confidence]] 的「負向測試（agent identity denied）」、第 331 輪 [[aida-tix-anomaly-detection]] 的「一致性而非準確率」並讀）。**③ ⭐⭐⭐ **「VERIFIED 表示『被某一指定的驗證政策接受』而非普遍真理」是語義設計上最精確的一處**——**狀態生命週期逐字為 `UNKNOWN → OBSERVED → CORROBORATED → VERIFIED`，另有 `→ CONTESTED`、`→ RETRACTED`、`→ SUPERSEDED` 三個分支**；**逐字註明「`VERIFIED` means "accepted by a specified verification policy" — not universal truth.」**；**另有一句逐字「**Verification distinguishes cryptographic validity from factual truth.**」**⭐⭐ **「誰的政策、什麼時候的政策」決定了「已驗證」是什麼意思**——**這在保險的場景判定（如是否構成全損、是否屬承保事故）中同樣成立**（**⚠️ 不主張**該狀態機適用於任何保險流程**）。**④ ⭐⭐⭐ **「身份只由不變內容決定，改狀態不改身份」是資料建模上最值得記的一點**——**逐字「The PROOF identity is a SHA-256 hash of the canonical representation of the **immutable content** only: Protocol version … Claim (subject, predicate, object), Evidence records. **Mutable fields (status, observed_at, attestations) are excluded. Changing status does not change identity.**」**⭐⭐⭐ **「這條主張是什麼」與「它現在被如何對待」是兩件事**（可與第 331 輪 [[paco-uw]] 的「歷史表永不復寫」並讀——**兩者都靠**把可變與不可變分開**來支撐可審計性**；**⚠️ 不主張**該設計在所有場景都適用**）。**⑤ ⭐⭐⭐ **PROOF** is **an open protocol for machine-readable claims, evidence, attestations and verification lifecycle** (repository `bhayrv/proof`), with **measured Apache-2.0 licence (`LICENSE` measured 200 on main), ★2, Python as the primary language, a 651 KB repository, created and last pushed 2026-09-09** (**licence, star count and language measured via the GitHub search API; `LICENSE` confirmed by raw probe; both inside the thaw window**); **the README measures 8,060 bytes**. **⚠️ One scope point must be stated at the outset**: **"claims" here means machine-readable assertions, not insurance claims**; **the protocol is not insurance-specific, and its relevance to insurance is inferential** (**evidence travelling with a claim; AI output independently verifiable downstream**) — **the entry does not claim any direct connection to insurance** (**see note ① below**). It is the third of this round’s four takes on **separating "what I observed" from "what I therefore conclude"**, **and the only one that writes that boundary into the protocol as its first principle**.

Verifiable details (**all read verbatim from the README**): **the title reads verbatim "PROOF Protocol"**, **the full name verbatim "Protocol for Readable Object Origin and Facts"**, **and the positioning verbatim**: **"An open protocol for machine-readable claims, evidence, attestations, temporal context, and verification lifecycle."** ⭐⭐⭐ **Its second sentence, read verbatim, is the entry’s most important line**: **"PROOF does not decide what is true. It provides a portable structure that allows independent systems to evaluate claims and their supporting evidence."**; **and its shorter slogan reads verbatim "Evidence should travel with information."** **Its status reads verbatim "PROOF 0.2 — Development"**, **with the declaration verbatim**: **"This is an experimental protocol and reference implementation. It is not yet a finalized interoperability standard. Breaking changes may occur between development versions."**

For RIAA: **① ⭐⭐⭐ "PROOF does not decide what is true" is the strongest form of this round’s theme** — **the other three entries draw the boundary inside a system** (**machine learning handles perception, the LLM only writes the wording, a rule engine decides**), **whereas this one draws it at the protocol layer: the protocol only carries and preserves, and judgement is left to independent consumers who may disagree with one another** (**⚠️ the entry does not claim that stance is workable in practice — its specification was not read**). **② ⭐⭐⭐ A whole "What PROOF Does NOT Claim" section reads verbatim, the most complete self-limitation of a new technology this session has seen** — **four items verbatim**: **"PROOF does not determine universal or factual truth."**; **"A cryptographic signature proves key control and data integrity — not that the claim is true."**; **"PROOF does not require blockchain, tokens, or centralized services."**; **"PROOF is an open infrastructure protocol, not an application."** ⭐⭐⭐ **The second deserves memorising: a cryptographic signature proves key control and data integrity, not that the claim is true — a necessary clarification in a setting where "signed" is easily misread as "proven"** (**readable with round 330’s [[claim-to-confidence]] and its negative test in which an agent identity is denied, and round 331’s [[aida-tix-anomaly-detection]] and its "agreement and disagreement, not accuracy" — all three sever a link between something that looks like proof and the conclusion actually wanted**). **③ ⭐⭐⭐ "VERIFIED means accepted by a specified verification policy, not universal truth" is the entry’s most precise semantic design point** — **the status lifecycle reads verbatim `UNKNOWN → OBSERVED → CORROBORATED → VERIFIED` with three further branches `→ CONTESTED`, `→ RETRACTED`, `→ SUPERSEDED`**; **and it notes verbatim "`VERIFIED` means \"accepted by a specified verification policy\" — not universal truth."**, **with a further line verbatim: "Verification distinguishes cryptographic validity from factual truth."** ⭐⭐ **For students of underwriting or compliance, whose policy and when determine what "verified" means — which also holds for insurance scenario determinations such as whether a total loss has occurred or an event is covered** (**⚠️ the entry does not claim the state machine suits any insurance process**). **④ ⭐⭐⭐ That identity is decided by immutable content alone, so changing status does not change identity, is the entry’s most notable data-modelling point** — verbatim: **"The PROOF identity is a SHA-256 hash of the canonical representation of the immutable content only: Protocol version (`\"proof\": \"0.2\"`), Claim (subject, predicate, object), Evidence records. Mutable fields (status, observed_at, attestations) are excluded. Changing status does not change identity."** ⭐⭐⭐ **For students of audit or versioning this is a clean invariant: "what this claim is" and "how it is currently being treated" are two different things, and the latter can change repeatedly while the former does not** (**readable with round 331’s [[paco-uw]] and its never-overwritten history table — both rest auditability on separating the mutable from the immutable**; **⚠️ the entry does not claim the design fits every setting — appending evidence would change identity, and its migration practice was not checked**). **⑤ ⭐⭐⭐ That contradictory claims may coexist is written into the relationship types** — **the graph relationships read verbatim as**: **`supports` / `corroborates`**; **"`contradicts` — conflicting claims (both can coexist)"**; **`supersedes`**; **`derived_from`**; **with a further line verbatim**: **"It represents exactly what was claimed, what evidence was associated with it, who attested to the exact immutable payload, and what supports or contradicts it."** ⭐⭐⭐ **This matches round 331’s [[paco-uw]], where both strategies’ results survive even when they contradict each other — the same attitude of not dissolving the contradiction but recording it** (**⚠️ the entry does not claim the design resolves evidential conflicts; it merely prevents them from disappearing**). **⑥ ⭐⭐⭐ `demo_ai_agent_pipeline.py` is the entry’s most directly AI-governance-related item** — verbatim: **"`demo_ai_agent_pipeline.py` — Simulates an AI extraction workflow: mock extraction → evidence association → review → attestation → deterministic verification, allowing downstream systems to verify the claimed provenance and attestation integrity without trusting the AI model itself."** ⭐⭐⭐ **Highly cognate with a theme that recurs across this site** (**per-field grounding in round 329’s [[reinsurance-treaty-agent]], an independent oracle and append-only audit log in round 330’s [[claim-to-confidence]], and a benchmark deliberately excluded from the feature matrix in round 331’s [[aida-tix-anomaly-detection]]**); **what this entry adds is a standardised form** (**⚠️ the example was not run**). **⑦ ⭐⭐ Its other three examples read verbatim and all concern claims changing over time**: **`demo_financial_intelligence.py`** (**an earnings claim, multiple evidence attachments, an attestation, and a later contradictory claim with a `contradicts` relation**); **`demo_temporal_supersession.py`** (**an acquisition claim revised via `supersedes`**, **noting verbatim "how a machine can trace claim history and apply an explicit consumer policy to identify the currently preferred claim"**); **`visualizer/index.html`** (**a dependency-free HTML/JS graph visualiser**); **and `cli_end_to_end.ps1`**. **⑧ ⭐⭐ Its security-model section reads verbatim and has three limits complementing "don’t mistake a signature for truth"**: **"Signatures prove key control and data integrity, not factual truth."**; **"Private keys are never persisted by the library."**; **"Timestamps are self-reported metadata, not cryptographically bound."**; **"The protocol is experimental."** ⭐⭐ **The third deserves separate note: timestamps are self-reported metadata and not cryptographically bound — that someone said something at some time is itself not guaranteed by cryptography** (**for students of audit trails, an easily overlooked weak point**). **⑨ ⭐⭐ Its interoperability section names six real standards, the entry’s most checkable point on the standards ecosystem**: **`docs/interoperability.md` reads verbatim "How PROOF maps to W3C PROV, C2PA, Verifiable Credentials, Sigstore, in-toto, and Schema.org"**; **with `docs/architecture.md` (covering the immutable identity model and canonicalisation strategy) and `spec/PROOF.md` (the normative specification)** ⭐⭐ **these are existing standards that can be independently checked** (**⚠️ the entry does not claim the mapping is accurate or complete — that document was not read**). **⑩ ⭐ Its CLI and Python API read verbatim and both stress strict pipeline compatibility**: **`proof create` (`--subject`, `--predicate`, `--object`, `--evidence-type`, `--evidence-source`), `proof inspect`, `proof identity`, `proof keygen`, `proof sign --private-key`, `proof verify`**, **with the note verbatim "All commands support JSON input/output for strict pipeline compatibility."**; **the Python API includes `Claim`, `Evidence`, `Proof`, `proof_id`, `create_attestation`, `verify_attestation`, `verify_proof`, `Attestation` and `result.to_dict()`**; **Python 3.11+ is required**. **⑪ ⭐ The detail that the version participates in identity computation reads verbatim**: **"The version participates in identity computation — the same claim under different versions has different identities."** — **⚠️ for a self-described experimental protocol that may still make breaking changes, this means identity is unstable across versions** (**the entry does not claim it suits long-term archival identifiers**). **⑫ ⭐ Readable with the site’s provenance, audit and AI-governance entries**: [[claim-to-confidence]], [[insurance-governance]], [[reproducible-actuarial-work]], [[verified-reserving]], [[rag-assurance]], [[powmcp-skills]], [[underwriting-decision-safety]], [[brel-xbrl]], [[risk-data-library-standard]].

⚠️ **Stated plainly**: **① ⚠️ Scope must be stated clearly: this repository is a general-purpose protocol for machine-readable claims and evidence provenance, not an insurance tool, and its README never mentions insurance**; **its relevance here is this entry’s inference — that "evidence travels with the claim" and "downstream systems can verify claimed provenance without trusting the AI model" have general significance for claims evidence chains and AI output auditing**; **the entry labels that relevance as inference and does not claim any direct connection, fit or adoption in insurance**; **②** this check verified **the repository metadata (partly via the search API), and the README’s full 8,060 bytes covering its definition, status declaration, problem statement, core data model, four "does not claim" items, status lifecycle, identity computation, graph relationships, quickstart, Python API, example list, development and security model, versioning, architecture/interoperability/specification pointers and licence**, **and confirmed by raw probe that `LICENSE` exists (HTTP 200)**, ⭐⭐ **but did not clone, install, run its CLI or Python API, run pytest, read `spec/PROOF.md` or anything under `docs/`, run any example, open its visualiser, or read `SECURITY.md` or any source**, so **its canonicalisation strategy, signature and verification implementation, graph data structures and any output cannot be restated**; **② ⭐⭐⭐ Whether the self-positioning "PROOF does not decide what is true" holds in the implementation was not verified** — **for example whether `verify_proof` really performs only cryptographic and policy determination without introducing semantic judgement**; **the source was not read**; **this is the single most important thing to verify next for this entry**; **③ ⭐⭐⭐ Whether the identity invariant "changing status does not change identity" holds was not verified**, **nor the actual behaviour of version-participates-in-identity or of appending evidence**; **④ ⭐⭐ Whether its mapping to W3C PROV, C2PA, Verifiable Credentials, Sigstore, in-toto and Schema.org is accurate or complete was not verified** (**`docs/interoperability.md` was not read**); **⑤ ⭐⭐ Whether its Ed25519 signing, key management and timestamp handling are secure was not verified** — **⚠️ it states that private keys are never persisted and that timestamps are self-reported and not cryptographically bound**; **the entry does not claim it resists any particular threat** (**no security assessment was performed**); **⑥ ⭐⭐ Whether its four examples (especially `demo_ai_agent_pipeline.py`) run or behave as described was not verified**;
